correctness.rationale: For the stated open neighborhoods in the incidence graph of a finite simple graph, nonempty edge-center traces live only in A and count e_A+lambda_A. The original-vertex centers give nonempty stars on B; if two distinct vertices have the same nonempty star, every edge in it must join those vertices, so simplicity makes them the two endpoints of an isolated marked K2. Subtract one duplicate per such component from |V(H_B)| and use the component Euler formula to get b+p_B-beta_B. The two supports are disjoint except for the separately counted empty trace. All upper-bound deficits are nonnegative; the clique with a helper and separate marked forest saturates them. Adding unmarked edges joining components preserves the saturated terms and a helper outside the marked-edge endpoints witnesses the empty trace, including the single-sort cases. In an extremal marked forest, the components with at least two edges consume all b edges in pairs except for at most one excess edge. The excess is itself a K2 or is absorbed in a three-edge tree, necessarily a claw or P4. Counting vertices gives the claimed minima. Pairing named edge labels gives the even census; in the odd minimum, choose the triple and its claw or one of three middle edges of P4, and pair the rest. Finally for m=a+b the pure A maximum dominates since b(2m-b+1)/2 >= 3b/2 for m>=2; for m=1 check both splits directly. The K2-marked-original construction shatters a pair, while no triple has eight traces. Inspected the supplied checker and recorded output, not executed. It makes 40,000 random draws, skipping empty markings, rather than checking 40,000 nonempty random cases; the reported combined 50,260 checks and the infinite proof do not rely on that wording.
